title: AI Literacy: Training, Bias and Honest Use
subject: digital

sections.body: AI systems learn from huge amounts of data. If the data is unbalanced, the AI can be BIASED. For example, a face-recognition system trained mostly on some groups may work worse for others.
AI can generate text, images and code, but it can be confidently wrong and it doesn't understand like a human.
Using AI honestly: follow your school's rules, say when you used it, use it to explain and give feedback rather than do your work, and check facts it gives you.

quiz.q: Why might an AI system be biased?
hints: If the training data leaves people out…
If you only learned about animals from a book about dogs, you'd know little about cats.
quiz.explain: AI can be biased when its training data is unbalanced or unrepresentative.

quiz.q: Which is an honest way to use AI for homework (where allowed)?
options: Ask it to explain a concept, then do the work yourself
Copy its essay and hand it in
hints: Which choice still helps you learn?
Using it as a tutor, not a ghost-writer.
Asking a friend to explain a math method is fine; copying their answers isn't.
quiz.explain: Use AI to understand, then do the work yourself, and be open about using it.
